findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. This filter excludes undismissed findings below the bar when their Harm is below 3. The new test supplies a Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1 finding and expects it to be absent, although `score.open_findings` still treats it as open. The stop question therefore omits a finding that Accept would dismiss and cannot show its promised “live with” outcome.
findings.title: Not done: every stop question shows the open notes

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The new owner-only rule conflicts with the guide's instruction to ask the human whenever a read or review loop stops. A repeated at-bar finding with Harm 1 or 2 triggers `close.py`'s review-loop stop and a human question; the guide then has the coordinator wait for a choice or the 30-minute default. This does not settle the note itself and tell the owner afterward.
findings.title: Not done: coordinator settles reversible Harm 1 and 2 notes itself

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The review and read examples each have only one row per bar outcome. Their assertions still pass if ranking ignores the required Harm-descending, Gain-descending and Work-ascending keys within an outcome. Neither command path checks the required bullet fallback when an open row is unscored. The named proof therefore misses specified table behavior.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The README says the question shows one ranked table, while the same page acknowledges that earlier-release notes have no scores. For an existing repo stopped on an unscored saved finding, `score.table` returns bullets instead. The delivered explanation gives that supported upgrade case the wrong output.

Raise: Gate. The supplied commit-message evidence says the worker's last commit has no `Functional check:` paragraph. This user-facing change therefore lacks the required account of exercising its covered behavior.
